title: Booking-time predictors of same-day discharge after elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy
subtitle: Choosing between existing records and prospective collection for a booking-time prediction model
statement: At a regional hospital performing about 620 elective laparoscopic cholecystectomies a year, 42 percent of patients booked as day cases stay overnight, often after late conversion. The day surgery unit wants booking-time predictors to plan list position and overnight stays in advance. The investigator planned a retrospective chart review of 2019 to 2025; the anaesthesia chief argues for prospective collection because charts record nausea severity and mobilisation poorly. The study must choose its data source, avoid overfitting, handle list position and surgeon effects, and produce something booking nurses can use.
whoAffected: Adults having elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, especially older patients and those living alone or far away; booking nurses, surgeons, anaesthetists and the day surgery unit.
whatHurts: Late conversion to an overnight stay frustrates patients who arranged to go home, disrupts the ward and wastes day-case capacity.
currentPractice: All suitable patients are booked as day cases; list order is set by surgeon preference; overnight stays are decided in the evening.
whyNow: A 2028 scheduling cycle, a data access approval and an analyst assigned in 2026.
constraints: No research funding; one decision support analyst for about 20 days; recommendations are needed for the day surgery unit's 2028 scheduling cycle; any prospective data collection would need nursing time that is not yet funded.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients know at booking whether they are likely to go home the same day and can plan for it.
summary: Problem framed as a booking-time prediction study with the data source to be decided.
